test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 23 Jan 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Kesavananda Bharti Case in 1973 stemmed the question that the Preamble can _______.
solution:
The correct answer is__** be amended**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kesavananda Bharti Case**

 
 
• The **Kesavananda Bharati case**, which established the basic structure theory of the Indian Constitution, is a **landmark judgment of the Supreme Court of India**. 
 
• The landmark decision was made on **April 24th, 1973, by a narrow majority of 7:6**.
 
• It holds that any **provision of the Indian Constitution can be amended by the Parliament in order to fulfil its socio-economic obligations** that were guaranteed to the citizens as stated in the Preamble
 
• It provides that such an amendment** did not alter the Constitution's fundamental structure**.
 
• However, the **minority had a divergent view** and cautioned against handing the Parliament unrestricted altering authority.
 
• The court ruled that the **24th Constitutional Amendment was fully lawful**.
 
• But it deemed the **second section of the 25th Constitutional** Amendment to be excessive.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kesavananda Bharati**

 
 
• He fought against the **Kerala land reforms Act**, which placed limitations on the management of religious property, **in 1970**.
 
• The ability to administer religiously owned property independently of the government was in dispute in this case under **Article 26**. 
 
• The Supreme Court assembled the** largest-ever bench of 13 judges** to hear the case.
 
 
 
• The case had been heard for **68 days**.
 
• The Kesavananda Bharati case, which had a severe dispute between the government and the judiciary, is popularly referred to as the **fundamental rights case.**
